Monkey Island 2: LeChuck's Revenge - Special Edition

fields.name: Mêlée Island
fields.description:
Mêlée Island was one of the main islands of the Tri-Island Area and served as the main home of its Governors.
Mêlée Island was also a popular place for the pirates of the Caribbean, and many settled there while LeChuck terrorized the seas. Many homes were near the dock and main street, while more were dotted around the island including tourism spots.

fields.name: Monkey Island
fields.description:
Monkey Island was a mystical legendary island located in the south eastern region of The Tri-Island Area.

Surrounding it was a voodoo mist. Most who travelled there believed a magical recipe was required to pass through. Elaine Marley had an alternate route to avoid it.

It was often used as the base of operations for the undead pirate LeChuck and his minions, but also was home to a tribe of Cannibals, Herman Toothrot, a large population of monkeys, and vultures.

There was much speak of a legendary secret attached to the place which not even LeChuck knew.

fields.name: Booty Island
fields.description: Booty Island was a major island of the Tri-Island Area. It was governed by Elaine Marley. It has a French influence and the inhabitants celebrated Mardi Gras all year round. Guybrush Threepwood visited the island in search of the map pieces to Big Whoop.

fields.name: Dinky Island
fields.description:
Dinky Island is a small island east of Monkey Island and also surrounded by the same mystic Voodoo fog. Much of the island consists of a curious jungle, with landmarks such as topiary sculpture.

Dinky was one of the islands of the Tri-Island Area that was interconnected by underground tunnels. The tunnels also were connected to the Mêlée Town.

It was the location where the crew of The Elaine hid the treasure of Big Whoop under a big X. Afterwards they ripped the treasure map and each one kept a piece.

In the book Big Whoop: Unclaimed Bonanza or Myth it was mis-labelled as "Inky Island" and captain Kate Capsize calls it "Blinky Island". The Men of Low Moral Fiber called it Drinky Island.

Also appears in The curse of Monkey Island

fields.name: Phatt Island
fields.description: Phatt Island was one of the main bodies of land nestled within the Tri-Island Area. It was ruled over by the facist dictator Governor Phatt. Guybrush Threepwood visited Phatt Island while searching for a map piece. He was taken prisoner by the Governor, but quickly escaped.

fields.name: Scabb Island
fields.description:
Scabb Island is an island in The Tri-Island Area. According to a book in the Phatt City Library, Scabb was first settled as a quarantine island for skin diseases. It later became a haven for pirates as there were no governors or any other authorities, the only island where Pirates were free to be pirates.

The main settlement was a town built from shipwrecks on the northern coast named Woodtick. Most residents lived there, though a few isolated homes were dotted around other island locations, such as the Peninsula and the swamp.

fields.name: Blood Island
fields.description: Blood Island was an island in the Tri-Island Area close to the storm surrounding Monkey Island. Guybrush Threepwood visited in order to find a diamond ring that could counteract the curse on Elaine Marley.

fields.name: Plunder Island
fields.description:
Plunder Island is one of the major locations in Curse of Monkey Island. It was part of the Tri-Island Area which made it under Governor Elaine Marley's purvey. 
The island was well regarded as a retirement community for ex-pirates and their spouses. It has/had an indigenous population but other than saying "Pappapisshu" instead of "ouch", there is nothing else known about them. It was also known for its large population of feral chickens, which led to the island town's name, Puerto Pollo. 

The Plunder Island Naturalist Society documents everything abou the wildlife of the island.
A song called Plunder on my Mind was written about the island.

fields.name: Skull Island
fields.description:
Skull Island is a small island off the coast of Blood Island and the hideout of the notorious smuggler King Andre, and his right hand man, Cruff. The only way to the island was to charter the local ferryman, known as the Flying Welshman, who knew how to navigate the sea's treacherous mists.

Though Skull Island is thought to look like a skull, it is revealed to the player that the island actually has the appearance of a duck. Guybrush even comments: "It should be called Duck Island". The Welshman insists that one must "squint and turn [one's] head a bit to see the skull". Guybrush continues to point out that if one actually does that, "it looks like a bunny". This is a reference to the famous rabbit-duck illusion, a kind of ambiguous drawing that causes the brain to be uncertain if the drawing illustrates a rabbit or a duck.

fields.name: Jambalaya Island
fields.description:
Jambalaya Island was once a pirate infested land where the Ultimate Insult was made. It has been currently industrialized into a pirate themed resort, complete with a Micro-Groggery and a StarBuccaneers. 

The pirates that have not yet been depiratized were deported to the nearby Knuttin Atoll, prevented from returning to the island by Admiral Ricardo Casaba. The island is also the host of a diving competition southeast to the town, as well as Stan's Timeshare Emporium.

fields.name: Lucre Island
fields.description:
Lucre Island was an island in The Tri-Island Area.

Guybrush Threepwood journeyed to the island in order to enlist the Marley Family lawyers in order to save the Governor's Mansion on Mêlée Island from being demolished.

fields.name: Gulf of Melange
fields.description: Gulf of Melange is the location of islands featured in Tales of Monkey Island.

fields.name: Boulder Beach
fields.description: Boulder Beach was an island within the Gulf of Melange which only featured a small rocky beach area. it is one of the islands explored by Guybrush in Tales of Monkey Island.

fields.name: Brillig Island
fields.description: Brillig Island was an island that is a part of the Gulf of Melange. It only featured a small beach area with some rocks and a coconut. There is a Rubber Tree here. It is also where Killick Hardtack and Murkel Trenchfoot buried the Noble Seahorse summoning artifact.

fields.name: Flotsam Island
fields.description:
Flotsam Island is a jungle-covered island in the Gulf of Melange that was explored by Guybrush Threepwood in Tales of Monkey Island.
The winds on the island, mysteriously blowing all inwards, meant that anyone who landed there would be unable to sail away. The Island is also surrounded by crystal reefs that tears up the ships that are being caught in the winds.

The island also have a large hidden temple of the Vacaylians, the ancient inhabitants of the island.

fields.name: Isle of Ewe
fields.description:
The Isle of Ewe was an island that consisted of a small beach and little else.
Guybrush Threepwood explored it searching for a buried summoning artifact.

The name often confuses people sounding like the phrase 'I love you'.

fields.name: Jerkbait Islands
fields.description:
The Jerkbait Islands were a series of three island within the Gulf of Melange. These consist of Roe Island, Spinner Cay and Spoon Island.

Roe island consited was basically a small beach island that was the substitue home of Coronado De Cava during his search for the La Esponja Grande.

Spinner Cay is the centre of the merfolk civilization known as the Vaycaylians in the Gulf of Melange. They were migrants from Flotsam Island, where some of their race left the water to worship the wind gods.

Spoon Island is similar to Flotsam Island, consisting of jungles and ancient Vacaylian ruins.

fields.name: Rock of Gelato
fields.description:
The Rock of Gelato was a small island rock complete with a sandy beach.
For unknown reasons, it is named after gelato, a type of ice cream.
The name may be a pun on the Rock of Gibraltar.

fields.name: Barebones Island
fields.description: Barebones Island was a small island that was somewhere north of Mêlée Island.

fields.name: Brrr‑Muda Island
fields.description:
Brrr Muda Island is an island north of Mêlée Island and the 19th Parallel.

It is a frozen landscape with its own system of government, different to that of the Tri-Island Area. Brrr Muda has a queen, who is not voted for, or comes through royal lineage. Instead, new queens are crowned after they defeat the current queen in three challenges, proving their right to rule.

Queen Odina would however visit Mêlée Island to discuss politics with the leaders there, her friends, Carla and Elaine Marley.

fields.name: Scurvy Island
fields.description:
Scurvy Island was a location in the Caribbean just north of Mêlée Island.
It was used by Elaine Marley as her base of operations for STAPL. She covered almost the entire island in lime groves in an attempt to combat scurvy.

In the past she and Guybrush Threepwood had also enjoyed romantic excursions to the various locations and sights it offered.

fields.name: Terror Island
fields.description:
Terror Island is a location that most pirates fear to tread.
It's landscape was frightening and mysterious. Bones littered the paths and clearings.

Guybrush Threepwood visited during his search for the secret of Monkey Island as he had been told that one of the five Golden Keys had been lost there.

fields.name: Guybrush Threepwood
fields.description:
Guybrush Ulysses Threepwood is the main protagonist of the Monkey Island series. He was first introduced in the Secret of Monkey Island as an ambitious, though somewhat naive wannabe-pirate. By the series' end, he had established himself as a competent swashbuckler. He would regularly be voiced by Dominic Armato.

Guybrush's chief nemesis was the dreaded undead pirate LeChuck, whom he faced throughout various installments of the series. At one point in LeChuck's Revenge, it was suggested that the two were brothers, which has since been brushed aside.

After a long and tempestuous courtship, Guybrush eventually married the woman he loved, Elaine Marley. The two had several more adventures together, which culminated with Tales of Monkey Island.

He had a number of talents and idiosyncrasies, the most well-known of which was his ability to stay underwater for ten minutes. When challenged to a duel, he was shown to play the banjo quite proficiently. He was also seen to be able to speak Spanish. He developed an irrational fear of porcelain.

He also had a talent for writing, and recorded his adventures in his own memoirs, which he often published.

Little is known of Guybrush Threepwood's true origins. As a kid he loved to collect fireflies in a jar.[1] He also had a Stretchy Strongman toy. He once mentioned that he (or rather his sister) owned a dolls house. He also admitted to having stopped practicing piano, which was strongly encouraged by his mother. He also had an abusive brother, Chuckie. One time he caused a serious accident involving scissors and his aunt's poodle, and he avoided dog grooming ever since.

In a hallucination he accused his parents for abandoning him.

When Guybrush first encountered the fiery Governor Elaine Marley, he revealed his troubled past with talking to women.

fields.name: Elaine Marley
fields.description:
Elaine Marley–Threepwood was the Governor of the Tri-Island Area. Her gubernatorial powers covered Mêlée Island, Booty Island and Plunder Island though she had some influence in a number of other locations too.

She was an able sailor and a captain of her own ship and crew. She was a resourceful and intelligent woman. She became the object of obsession by the zombie pirate LeChuck, which led her into situations where she fell into becoming the damsel in distress. More often than not however, she was perfectly capable of escaping and handling herself. In combat, she was an accomplished swordswoman and could throw a rather dangerous punch.

She was the favourite relative of her grandfather Horatio Torquemada Marley, who named his ship The Elaine after her. She was likely the only person whom he confided to regarding the truth behind Dinky Island and Big Whoop.

She later married her longtime romantic interest, the legendary pirate Guybrush Threepwood. Following the events of Escape from Monkey Island, she handed her gubernatorial duties back to her estranged grandfather.

fields.name: LeChuck
fields.description:
LeChuck, sometimes officially known as G.P. LeChuck is arguably the most fearsome pirate ever to sail the seven seas. He was a skilled swordsman, a ruthless killer and a master of manipulation.

He had an obsession with voodoo and the occult, even to the point where he turned himself into an undead abomination in order to harness greater power.

As a man he had a crew of hardy, loyal and cutthroat buccaneers, but when he became an undead horror, his powers grew and his subordinates became almost immortal.

His weakness was his hopeless love of Elaine Marley, the Governor of the Tri-Island Area. Rumour has it that when she told him to 'drop dead' he took it literally. Since then, he has strived to make her his undead bride.

According to Largo LaGrande LeChuck did not give tips.

In his later years, he became the arch nemesis of Guybrush Threepwood.

According to the Voodoo Lady, his reason for being was "to perpetually rise from the dead and torment you and Elaine. It's what he does best."

Since the whole game story is about LeCuck, Guybrush and Elaine Marley, Lechuck demands a little more attention and details about his origin.
When LeChuck was still alive, he was a fearsome bloodthirsty pirate. He met and fell in love with the Governor of Mêlée Island, Elaine Marley when he had been invited to her mansion for a dinner.

She was not enamoured with him though and told him to "drop dead" in response to his advances. LeChuck took this quite literally and was supposedly killed by a storm when he was searching for the Secret of Monkey Island. But his black spirit and love for Elaine was enough for him to resurface as a vengeful ghost who haunted the seas. His victims were killed, turned into living skeletons and ghosts and then forced to join his crew. This made many pirates afraid of the ocean and, as LeChuck puts it, "too afraid to take a bath".

fields.name: Carla
fields.description:
Carla, better known as the Sword Master of Mêlée Island, was a master swordsman and one of the pirates Guybrush Threepwood has to defeat to attain his status as a bonafide pirate. She was a fierce warrior and lived deep in the forest of the island in an attempt to avoid people from constantly challenging her title. Only the storekeeper in town knew where she hid, which allowed Guybrush to seek her out.

She was initially trained by Captain Smirk, before her skills surpassed his. Her talent lay with her wit and an uncanny ability to think up original insults that few could ever challenge.

fields.name: Herman Toothrot
fields.description:
Horatio Torquemeda Marley was a famous Captain and adventurer, well regarded throughout the Caribbean. He was also the elected Governor of the Tri-Island Area, though that didn't stop him from satiating his hunger for seeking dangerous thrills around the world. He fell victim to the machinations of the evil pirate LeChuck during his search for the legendary treasure of Big Whoop. He and his crew returned home, unable to speak of the atrocities they witnessed.

He would later be known as Herman Toothrot, after he lost his memory in an unfortunate accident. He then lived the life of a hermit for several years on Monkey Island, unable to remember one iota of his past. In Escape from Monkey Island, Guybrush Threepwood helped him recover his memories. This drove Horatio to seek revenge against LeChuck and Ozzie Mandrill, and put a stop to their plans.

He was the grandfather of Elaine Marley, who would later relinquish her gubernatorial powers to him after he recovered his memories, and returned to Mêlée Island.

fields.name: Meathook
fields.description:
Meathook is a resident on Hook Island, which was situated northeast the coast of Mêlée Island. He had two hooks instead of hands, because they were bitten off by a parrot which he named a "ferocious beast" when he was 30 years younger. He also lost an eye to the parrot. Though that parrot was long gone, he kept a smaller one called the Beast locked away in his home.
He ran a hotel in his home on Hook Isle, though ironically, he did not like visitors. His attractions included animal acts, tattoo demonstrations and souvenirs. He was put out of business however when a guest was badly hurt by the Beast.

He was a man of many talents. He was a ventriloquist and used his skill with the skull-shaped tattoo so that it appears to be talking. He named it Roger.

Later he put Guybrush Threepwood to touch the Beast in order to agree to join his crew on the Sea Monkey in order to sail ot Monkey Island and save Governor Elaine Marley from LeChuck.

fields.name: Murray
fields.description:
Murray is a Demonic Skull that terrorized Guybrush Threepwood who first appeared the Curse of Monkey Island. He was originally part of LeChuck's Army of the Undead, before losing his entire skeletal body, and becoming somewhat independent.
Despite his predicament, he always thought of ways to terrorize others, which often ended in personal injury or embarrassment. 
He described himself as an object of pure evil, and dreamed of spreading chaos throughout the Caribbean. He became one of the more memorable characters of the series, appearing in cameo roles in later installments.

fields.name: Otis
fields.description: Otis is a local thief, who was known to have very bad case of halitosis. He tended to whine a lot, and would often bemoan his predicament. This tended to test the patience of those around him, especially considering his oral condition. He was seemingly of Spanish in origin, sporting a full beard. Later versions of Monkey Island gave him a unique accent.

fields.name: Stan
fields.description: Stan S. Stanman is a fast-talking, eccentric salesman in The Tri-Island Area who made regular appearances throughout the series. Whether he liked it or not, he often found himself dealing with Guybrush Threepwood as he went on with his adventures. This led to Stan being in fairly compromising or uncomfortable situations. He harbored no ill-will, however, and would gladly deal with Guybrush more often than not.

fields.name: Voodoo Lady
fields.description:
Corina, better known as The Voodoo Lady, is a well-known traveling mambo (Voodoo Priestess) and self-proclaimed fashion consultant. She has provided invaluable advice to Guybrush Threepwood throughout the series, thanks to her extensive knowledge with voodoo curses, magic and the occult. She claimed to have clairvoyance, able to predict Guybrush's fate and actions a number of times throughout the series. She was also attuned with the Force and could sense events happening away.

She was a fairly large woman with a dark complexion. She liked to speak in a dramatic fashion, particularly when it had something to do with Guybrush's quest. She often spoke in riddles and obscure phrases, never quite giving the answers Guybrush needed to fully comprehend his situation. She clearly knew what's good for Guybrush, which has helped him out more times than he could remember.

Her stores were often similarly themed, with large draperies to the sides and a large pot of voodoo potions or soup at arm's length. She has never been known to stay put in one island for very long, and likes to move her operations around the Caribbean when she felt like it.

fields.name: Wally
fields.description:
Wally B. Feed was a cartographer on Scabb Island. He wore a monocle and was unable to see without it.

He claimed to have traveled all the world, and putting every place he'd seen on paper. As well as making maps, he did restoration work on them, repairs, copying and 'artsy fartsy stuff' like painting little cupids in the corners.

His mother passed away some time before he met Guybrush Threepwood on Scabb Island.

He was something of an expert on Big Whoop and was happy to help Guybrush put together the map pieces required to find it.

fields.name: Boybrush
fields.description:
Boybrush James Threepwood was the son of Guybrush Threepwood and Elaine Marley. Boybrush would often re-enact his father's adventures with his friend Chuckie in the Big Whoop Amusement Park.

At a point in time, Boybrush was told a tale of Guybrush's adventures.

fields.name: Captain Blondebeard
fields.description:
Captain Blondebeard is the proprietor of Blondebeard's Chicken Shop a chicken restaurant located near the center of Puerto Pollo, the main town of Plunder Island. While a kindly and warm individual, he nevertheless did not take criticism of his cooking lightly.

Blondebeard regarded himself a Connoisseur o' Carrion, and claimed to be a huge fan of his fried chicken recipe. One of the things he enjoyed most of his cooking was the crunchiness of the beaks between his teeth.

He has been a member of the Brimstone Beach Country Club and Smorgy since 1632, after threatening to run the management all through.

He greatly feared the dreaded El Pollo Diablo, otherwise known as "The Demon Chicken", and vowed revenge after his chickens were set free.

fields.name: Captain Smirk
fields.description:
Captain Smirk was an expert swordsman who taught his skill to worthy students in his home on Melee Island. It was known as 'Captain Smirk's Big Body Pirate Gym'. He was known for a signature sarcastic expression, which often his students would pick up from him.

Years ago he fought with Carla in Port Royal against the local constabulary forces; Carla later became the island's swordmaster.

He believed that a well placed insult could be the winning blow a fight. When he felt his students needed intense basic training, he would introduce The Machine: a device he built to test a swordfighter's skills.

He later trained Guybrush Threepwood (after he insisted too much) in use of the sword and the basics of Insult Sword Fighting.

fields.name: Domingo
fields.description:
Palido Domingo is an unusually pale-skinned talent manager, and could be found sunbathing in Brimstone Beach Country Club and Smorgy in Plunder Island. He comes off rather rude towards Guybrush, mistaking him for a waiter.

His longtime client was thespian and playwright Slappy Cromwell. The two shared a long working relationship back when Cromwell was performing on Blood Island. So long in fact, that Domingo had the map to Blood Island tattooed to his back.

fields.name: Fossey
fields.description:
Mr. Fossey is the unhinged first mate of Captain LeChimp aboard The Sea Cucumber, which itself had a crew entirely made of monkeys.

Mr. Fossey believed he could hear the voice of his captain, despite nobody else being able to. He had habit of hearing his master's call just as he was about to say his name. This meant many assuming he worked for the dreaded pirate LeChuck. Though, after Guybrush infiltrates the ship and discovers that the captain is actually an ape, he realizes that Mr. Fossey is nothing but "an utter loon".

He believed that the captain and his crew would use the golden statue of Elaine Marley they stole from the beach to buy an entire fleet of ships and become the ultimate terror of the Caribbean.

He was fond of chicken and occasionally ordered from Blondebeard's Chicken Shoppe.

fields.name: Haggis
fields.description:
Haggis McMutton of the Clan McMutton is a burly Scotsman with a thick accent. His given name was Heart Liver and Kidneys Boiled in the Stomach of the Animal McMutton, since his parents originally wanted a girl.

He has a great-aunt called Angus. He called his sword Old Ironsides.

fields.name: Kate Capsize
fields.description:
Captain Kate Capsize appeared in Monkey Island 2: LeChuck's Revenge. She was the attractive red-haired owner of a Ship Chartering Business and advertised her trade on Booty Island.

She drank near-grog (non-alcoholic grog) and was known to finish off the supplies at The Bloody Lip.

The Barkeeper described her as courageous, tough as nails, hard as steel. He said her loyalty is only to the highest bidder and warned against getting on her bad side.

Kate makes a cameo in the Pirates Life expansion of the game Sea of Thieves. In the game, five books can be found, that chronicle her search for Guybrush Threepwood after he framed her for his crimes in Monkey Island 2.

fields.name: Lagrande
fields.description:
Largo LaGrande was a Pirate and LeChuck's right hand man.

For a time he was in unofficial control of Scabb Island. Many pirates on Scabb Island feared him for his old connection to LeChuck more than his own merit. He bullied the inhabitants, took large amounts of their earnings and enforced an expensive embargo which left many pirates landlocked.

fields.name: LeChimp
fields.description:
Captain LeChimp is an average-looking gorilla, dressed in pirate attire. The deranged Mr. Fossey mistakenly imagined him as a fearsome captain and the leader of the Pirates of Danjer Cove.

LeChimp lived aboard the Sea Cucumber, which was moored in Danjer Cove. He was taken care of by Mr. Fossey along his crew of monkeys, who had hoped to improve their standing among pirating circles. Guybrush Threepwood tricked Mr. Fossey into leaving the profession of piracy and allow LeChimp and his associates to go back to nature.

He had a fearsome reputation due mainly to the mystery surrounding him and his crew. In fact, Guybrush initially assumed him to be LeChuck.

fields.name: Leflay
fields.description:
Morgan LeFlay is a fierce female pirate-hunter that appeared in Tales of Monkey Island. She was a long time admirer of the adventures of Guybrush Threepwood. This however, did not deter her from accepting a job from the Marquis De Singe to capture him for the scientist's experiments.

When she boarded the Screaming Narwhal, LeFlay cornered Threepwood and cut off his hand, prompting a sword duel with him.

fields.name: Pirate Leaders
fields.description:
The Very Important Pirate Leaders were frequent patrons of the Scumm Bar in Mêlée Town.

They had their own curtained off VIP area to show their importance. Their drink of choice was grog.

fields.name: Rottingham
fields.description:
Rene Rottingham was a fearsome scoundrel and pirate captain seen in The Curse of Monkey Island. He was a Frenchman and master swordsman and reputed to be the most cunning and well-groomed captain ever to sail the Caribbean.

An arrogant man, he was extremely proud of his hair, and would mock anyone with hair he deemed to look bad. He massaged his scalp lovingly with the finest creams and oils in the world, twice daily. He was willing to kill men for insulting his grooming.

His self importance had him boast that he would serve under no one elses command.

fields.name: Storekeeper
fields.description:
The Storekeeper of Mêlée Island was a gruff and grumpy 83-years old man who tended to his store located in the Mêlée Town. He walked with a limp and carried a walking cane to help him get about.

He was able to give credit to trusted customers. He was the only person who knew the location of the legendary Swordmaster of Mêlée Island when she went into hiding in the forest. He was a romantic admirer of hers, visiting her often, though she did not return the feelings.

When leaving the store unattended he had a knack for knowing if his bell had been rung or if anyone was attempting to steal anything.

When Guybrush Threepwood came to the island for the first time, the store keeper was 83 years of age.

fields.name: Van Helgen
fields.description:
Edward Van Helgen, better known as Snugglecakes, is one of "Bucaneer Hairstylists" Guybrush Threepwood encounters in the Barbery Coast. He was pirate of some infamy, having been on a number of well known adventures making his name feared. One such adventure had him aboard the doomed voyage of The Obsessivo-Compulsivo.

Edward felt that the sea had a music of its own and that many restless souls couldn't live life without it. But the sailor's life was so hard that he gave up this life when he realised one could enjoy the same music on dry land. He first spent some time at docks, singing to sailors passing-by, but this failed to satiate his musical needs.

Eventually he formed a barbershop quartet, which united him with Haggis McMutton, Cutthroat Bill and a tenor named Dominique.

He said he could never serve a captain who was not a gentleman and who was not his equal.

fields.name: Breathmaster
fields.description:
Breathmasters were a brand of grog flavoured mints. Rolls cost one Piece o' Eight.
Its slogan is "For the pirate who cares about first impressions".

They are sometimes referred to as 'Grog-o-mint'.

fields.name: Business Card
fields.description:
Stan's Business Card was given out by Stan to any visitors of his Previously-Owned Vessels store along with an Extra Strong Magnetic Compass.
Every pirate who wants to buy a vessel should really contact Stan Stansman!

fields.name: Compass
fields.description: The Extra Strong Magnetic Compass was a free gift from Stan's Previously-Owned Vessels for all new potential customers. It had a picture of Stan on it and always pointed to the store, so that buyers would know where to find a good deal.

fields.name: Jug of Grog
fields.description:
Every real pirate's possession is the good old grog.
Here in a form of a respectable amount in a jug.
The grog can also be referred to as rum.
See also mug of grog.

fields.name: Mug of Grog
fields.description:
In every pirate bar you can find pirates sitting with these mugs of grog.
A good example is the SCUMM bar which is the first place Guybrush visits when he begins his adventure.

fields.name: Pieces of Eight
fields.description:
Pieces o' Eight are the currency used throughout the Caribbean.
Just like in the real world you won't go very far without cash.
All pirates should have a bag of these, more or less.

fields.name: Rope
fields.description: A rope is a group of yarns, plies, fibres, or strands that are twisted or braided together into a larger and stronger form. Ropes have tensile strength and so can be used for dragging and lifting. Rope is thicker and stronger than similarly constructed cord, string, and twine.

fields.name: Shovel
fields.description:
A shovel was a useful tool for many pirates.

Its primary use was for digging up or burying treasure, though it was also useful for gravedigging.

fields.name: Spyglass
fields.description:
A spyglass or telescope is a tool used for looking over long distances, useful on board ships for navigation and looking for land as well as spotting other vessels.

Most captains will not be without one while at sea.

fields.name: Sword
fields.description:
Swords are a standard weapon used by pirates in the Caribbean.
They come in a number of styles, from rapiers to cutlasses.
They are predominantly used in the art of Insult Sword Fighting.
